newsitem.title: PERU: Telefonica del Peru sells 15 mln soles debt paper.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica del Peru sells 15 mln soles debt paper.

text.p: Telefonica del Peru officials said the company placed 15 million soles of short-term debt paper out of a total offer of 50 million soles at an auction on Thursday.
The officials said the instruments, the first tranche of a planned $180 million issue, had a 90-day maturity and 14.75 percent annual interest rate.
The issue is the first time a Peruvian company has placed short-term debt instruments, according to the Lima Stocks and Securities Board (CONASEV).
"Investors did not completely take up the offer because of the current lack of depth in the local market and because we are drawing to the end of the year," one of the officials said.
Local ratings agency Duff & Phelps del Peru had classifed the issue with its highest rating of DPp1+.

Last week, CONASEV gave Telefonica approval to make the $180 million issue over three years with instruments carrying a maximum maturity of one year. The income from the issue will be used to boost capital and for expansion and repair work, according to company officials.
The company also recently began an issue over three years of 250 million soles of corporate bonds.
The firm is majority-owned by Spain's Telefonica de Espana after its $2.002 billion privatization in 1994.
